findings.title: Fire-and-forget goroutines using request-scoped context without proper detachment
findings.body: In Create, Delete, Update, and DeleteCollection, the async legacy write goroutine does `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` using the original request ctx as parent. If the HTTP request context is cancelled/finishes (as it normally does once the response is returned to the client), the derived context is cancelled immediately, so the legacy write will likely fail with context canceled before the 10s timeout has a chance to elapse. This defeats the purpose of the async legacy write (reliability net) in mode 3, silently causing legacy writes to fail most of the time in production. The context passed to the goroutine should be detached from the parent request context (e.g., using `context.WithoutCancel` or a fresh context with request-scoped values copied) before adding the timeout.

findings.title: Metric label mix-up: name used instead of Kind, and errObjectSt naming inconsistency
findings.body: Line 106 (`d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)`) passes the deleted resource `name` where other calls pass `options.Kind` as the metric label; this is inconsistent with every other method in this file and will skew/break metric aggregation by kind for Delete operations.

findings.title: DeleteCollection records legacy result using recordStorageDuration instead of recordLegacyDuration
findings.body: In the goroutine for DeleteCollection, the legacy call's result is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`, unlike Create/Delete/Update which correctly call `recordLegacyDuration` for the async legacy write. This mislabels legacy write metrics as storage metrics, corrupting dashboards/alerts based on these metrics.

findings.title: No rollback/compensation when legacy write fails in mode 3 async path
findings.body: Because the legacy write happens asynchronously after the unified storage write succeeds, there's no mechanism (retry, dead-letter, reconciliation) to catch or compensate when the legacy write fails (errObjectSt != nil only gets fed into a metric, nothing else). Given this is explicitly described as a 'safe measure' for keeping legacy in sync, silently dropping failures could lead to drift between legacy and unified storage with no operator-visible signal besides a metric. The PR doesn't address detection/alerting/retry for this gap.

findings.title: No tests verify async legacy write behavior of mode 3
findings.body: All tests for mode3 only verify that the Storage (unified) call result is used/returned; none of the tests assert that the Legacy mock's Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection methods are actually invoked (asynchronously) with correct arguments, nor do they test the new timeout/cancellation behavior. Given mode3's entire purpose is to also write to legacy storage, this is a significant test gap — a regression that stops the async legacy write entirely would not be caught by this suite.
